title: 了 Step 3 · No 了 Here! Negation, Habits and States
description: Not every past sentence takes 了: 没 + verb never does, past habits don't, and verbs like 是, 喜欢, 觉得 usually don't.

points.title: 没 + verb: no 了
points.summary: The negative of a completed action is 没(有) + verb — without 了.
points.body:
- 我吃**了**早饭。 → 我**没**吃早饭。 (never ~~我没吃了早饭~~)
- 他来**了**吗？ — 他**没**来。
- Careful: 不…了 (not any more) is fine — that's sentence-了 (step 2).

**了 at a glance: done, or changed?**

| | where | means | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| verb-了 | right after the verb | **done** (completed action) | 我买**了**三本书。 |
| sentence-了 | end of the sentence | **changed** (new situation) | 下雨**了**。 我饿**了**。 |
| both | after the verb + at the end | **so far, and still going** | 我学**了**三年中文**了**。 |

**Where 了 does NOT go**
- With 没: 我**没**吃早饭 — never ~~没吃了~~.
- Habits and general states in the past: 我以前**常常**去, 他以前**是**老师, 我小时候**喜欢**画画.
- Plain description: 昨天很冷 — no 了 needed.

**Look-alikes:** 快 / 要 …了 = **about to** (快下雨了); 太…了 = **so / too** (太好了!) — no change involved.

points.title: Habits and states in the past: no 了
points.summary: Things that were usual or true over a period — 常常, 每天, 以前是, 喜欢 — don't take 了.
points.body:
- 我以前**每天**跑步。 I used to run every day.
- 他小时候**是**一个很安静的孩子。
- 我以前**喜欢**吃辣的。
- 昨天**很冷**。 (a description — no 了 needed)

**了 at a glance: done, or changed?**

| | where | means | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| verb-了 | right after the verb | **done** (completed action) | 我买**了**三本书。 |
| sentence-了 | end of the sentence | **changed** (new situation) | 下雨**了**。 我饿**了**。 |
| both | after the verb + at the end | **so far, and still going** | 我学**了**三年中文**了**。 |

**Where 了 does NOT go**
- With 没: 我**没**吃早饭 — never ~~没吃了~~.
- Habits and general states in the past: 我以前**常常**去, 他以前**是**老师, 我小时候**喜欢**画画.
- Plain description: 昨天很冷 — no 了 needed.

**Look-alikes:** 快 / 要 …了 = **about to** (快下雨了); 太…了 = **so / too** (太好了!) — no change involved.
examples: I used to go swimming every day.

notes: 没 + verb never takes 了.
不 + 了 after the verb doesn't work.

questions.explanation: Not yet: 还**没**来 (no 了).
notes: 不来了 = he's not coming any more — a change of plan, not 'not yet'.
questions.translation: A: Has he come? B: Not yet.

questions.prompt: 了 where it doesn't belong: right or wrong?
questions.explanation: No 了 with **没**, with **habits**, or when describing a past **state**.
notes: 没 already says it didn't happen — drop the 了.
Describing how it **was** → 昨天很冷, no 了 (很冷了 would mean 'it has got cold').
Habits (每天, 常常) don't take verb-了.
没 + verb, no 了 — right.

options: {他|tā}{小时候|xiǎoshíhou}{了|le}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{画画|huà huà}。
{他|tā}{小时候|xiǎoshíhou}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{了|le}{画画|huà huà}。
{他|tā}{小时候|xiǎoshíhou}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{过|guo}{了|le}{画画|huà huà}。
questions.explanation: States like 喜欢 in the past → **no 了**.
notes: 喜欢 (a lasting feeling) doesn't take verb-了 here.
questions.translation: As a child he loved drawing.

questions.prompt: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bàba}{以前|yǐqián}（　）{老师|lǎoshī}，{现在|xiànzài}{退休|tuìxiū}{了|le}。
questions.explanation: 是 in the past → **no 了**. (退休了 = retired now — a change.)
notes: 是 doesn't take 了 in the past.
了 doesn't go before 是.
questions.translation: My dad used to be a teacher — he's retired now.

questions.explanation: A description of the past: **很冷** — no 了 needed.
questions.translation: It was very cold yesterday — I wore two jumpers.

questions.prompt: 「{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}。」 vs 「{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。」 — what's the difference?
options: Both mean I'm not going any more.
没去 is future; 不去了 is past.
没去 = I didn't go; 不去了 = I'm not going any more (changed my mind).
questions.explanation: **没** + verb = didn't; **不…了** = not any more.
notes: 没去 is about what happened.
不去了 is a change of plan.

questions.prompt: 'I used to go swimming every day.' Which sentence says so?
questions.explanation: 以前 + 每天 = a habit → **no 了**.
notes: Sentence-了 would make it a new situation.
questions.translation: I used to go swimming every day.

questions.explanation: 没 + verb never takes 了.

questions.prompt: Why is there no 了 in 「{我|wǒ}{小时候|xiǎoshíhou}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{上海|Shànghǎi}。」?
options: It describes a situation over a period, not a single completed action.
Because 了 is never used with 住.
Because 上海 is a city.
questions.explanation: A lasting situation in the past → no 了 needed.
notes: 住了三年 is fine — 了 is possible with 住.
questions.translation: When I was little I lived in Shanghai.
